data: Iterative DFS does not guarantee the shortest path as it may find a deeper path first.
BFS is preferred for shortest path problems.

While BFS and Iterative DFS have
similar
time complexity,
their performance and efficiency vary based on the
problem context. BFS is better suited for level-based exploration and shortest-path problems, whereas Iterative DFS is
ideal for deep exploration, structural analysis, and solving puzzles or backtracking-based problems. Understanding the

nature of
the input data and the specific requirements of
the problem is essential
in choosing the most appropriate
